name: Thurenna
gloss: The Knot That Would Not Loose

anatomy.part: the eye of the hitch, on the edge of the inner turn where the right-hand tail leaves the knot body
upper left loop of the knot body, on the inner turn near the left edge
left edge of the knot body, on its rounded outline
tip of the upper rope end rising from the top of the knot
far tip of the long tail at the top left
outer left edge of the lower bight, where the standing part comes down into it
inner ring of the lower bight, along its top
right side of the bight, where the lower tail leaves it

myth: When Aun was a boy he tied his grandmother's hitch on the mooring post, and Tavo the Gale came down the Leeward sea to shake it loose. Tavo blew until the spray stood up like walls. The knot held. He blew harder and the boat spun on its rope, and still the knot held, for the old woman had pulled it tight with her teeth as well as her hands. Tavo laughed, a sound like a sail tearing, and went off to find an easier thing to break. Hesk saw the knot from the pole and wound it into the Leeward line, where it is tied yet at the far end of the sky. That is why we tie our boats with a grandmother's hitch. When a thing will not come undone we say it was tied properly. Do not try to loose it. Check your own knots before the wind comes.
verse:
Hesk counts the rope's turns
the grandmother's hitch held fast
still tied and still held
